messages:
Alex R: Quick handoff before I sign off — main items and coverage for the night. Root: no active Sev1s, but degraded request queueing in eu-central for a subset of customers.

Samira K: Taking primary now. I'll be primary until 07:00 CET. Who's listed as secondary?

Alex R: Maya is secondary until 01:15 CET, then we have a planned gap (holiday) and Ilya will be secondary only after 02:30 CET. That leaves 01:15-02:30 with no dedicated secondary on the roster. We discussed voluntary coverage earlier; if anything is paged as Sev1 in that window, treat as full-incident and escalate immediately to SRE manager.

Maya L: Confirmed secondary until 01:15. If the window opens, I can extend until 01:45 if needed, but need to warn my on-call family.

Ilya P: I'm good to take secondary after 02:30. I'll be remote and reachable by PD and phone.

Samira K: Noted. Procedural reminders for escalation (copying the runbook summary):
- Sev1 (system-wide customer outage): PagerDuty -> "sre-pager" (immediate). If no ack in 5m, call SRE manager on duty and sms + escalate to eng-lead on call.
- Sev2 (partial customer impact / high error rate): PagerDuty -> "eng-oncall". If no ack in 10m, post to #incidents and page runtime-lead.
- Sev3 (no customer impact / internal alarm): Slack thread monitoring only; create ticket in JIRA if flapping.

oncall-bot: Automated note: Please ack PD pages within 2 minutes. Failure to ack triggers escalation policy.

Alex R: Phone fallbacks in case PD/Slack fail: use the on-call phone tree. Step 1: try primary mobile (from roster), Step 2: call secondary mobile, Step 3: call SRE manager landline. If still unreachable, call the office ops number. DO NOT post private numbers in public channels — use DMs or the secure roster link.

Samira K: I'm adding an emergency sticky to the #incidents channel with the exact phone tree and a link to the secure roster. Also adding a note about customer communication owners. If CSE or PM escalations come in, tag @pm-rotations and @customer-success and include the customer-impact template.

Maya L: For the eu-central queueing issue: temporary mitigation is to ramp up worker pool and enable the short-concurrency fallback on the gateway. Run this snippet and annotate the incident thread: 
```
# temp scale for eu-central
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/api/scale -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_TOKEN}' -d '{"region":"eu-central","replicas":6}'
```
If that doesn't reduce queue depth in 8m, escalate to runtime team and attach the p99 latency histogram.

Ilya P: If PD page is not firing (we saw PD webhook throttling last month), use the PD CLI to trigger and then post the link. Example: `pd incident create --service runtime --title "Sev1: EU queueing" --severity 1`

Samira K: Adding a special-case for the coverage gap: if a Sev1 occurs between 01:15-02:30 CET, primary (me) should follow the full incident runbook AND immediately call SRE manager (listed in secure roster). If manager cannot be reached in 7m, call the on-call director. We cannot let a Sev1 linger due to the gap.

Alex R: Also logging that ML infra lead is OOO tonight. Model-level rollbacks/quant changes should be routed to runtime and tagged for ML infra the next business day. If customers demand immediate model rollback, run the gateway variant swap and document it.

oncall-bot: Incident template attached when a new Sev1 is created. Use `!inc create` to start.

Samira K: For communication cadence: update #incidents every 10m during an active Sev1, and every 30m for Sev2. Post a brief summary when status changes and CC the account owner's rotation if specific customers are affected.

Maya L: Note about PD escalation chains — sometimes the second-level escalation is set to the rotation group which is empty due to a holiday. If you hit an empty escalation target, immediately escalate to the human fallback (sre-manager) via phone. I filed a follow-up to make escalation targets robust.

Ilya P: I'll be ready to hop on a call if runtime needs to check kernel selection or KV cache saturation. Keep logs in the incident thread and include heatmap + `netstat -an` for connection counts.

Alex R: TL;DR handoff: Samira primary 01:00->07:00 CET, Maya secondary til 01:15 (maybe extend), coverage gap 01:15-02:30 (SRE manager fallback), Ilya secondary after 02:30. PagerDuty mandatory for Sev1/Sev2; phone tree for PD failure. Runbooks: https://confluence.redwood/ops/oncall/night-handbook and https://confluence.redwood/ops/oncall/pager-rules

Samira K: Taking handoff. I'll post check-ins at 23:00 and 02:00 CET and will keep this thread open. Ping me if anything pops. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Reminder scheduled: Nightly health check at 23:55 CET. Collecting service metrics now...
